text:
Maya: observability alert -> multiple runtime pods on gpu-pool-3 started crashing at 21:13 UTC with kernel page-walk faults. seeing node flaps and automated pod restarts. marking P1 for now.
IncidentBot: ALERT triggered: node/gpu-03 kernel OOPS: page walk address fault (gpu) — auto-created incident INC-2134.
Maya: quick snapshot: ~6 pods crashed across 3 nodes, spike in 502s from model-serving route /generate, tail of kubelet shows container runtime restart loops.
Jordan: oncall here — adding notes. can someone paste dmesg/kernel logs from affected nodes? I want to see exact fault string.
Priya: grabbing logs from gpu-03 now. suspecting page-walk address fault from GPU driver/kernel interaction after recent kernel patches. past incidents hinted at a race on page table migration.
Alex: will start cordoning and draining gpu-03/04/05 to reduce customer impact. recommending we move serving traffic to cpu-fallback nodes + dedicated fallback model until we have root cause.
Maya: Sam, can you check customer-facing dashboards? any customers with errors or latency anomalies?
Sam: customer telemetry shows 12 tenants with elevated error rates, 4 with >5% 502s in last 5m. CS is preparing a notice. severity: svc-impacting.
Priya: logs from gpu-03 (excerpt):
```
[ 2184.452334] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, GPU page fault at 0x7f2d3a4000
[ 2184.452338] kernel: page_walk: address 0x7f2d3a4000 caused PFN corruption, code 0x0
[ 2184.452340] containerd: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[ 2184.452345] stack trace:
  gpu_driver+0x1f4a3
  gpu_vm_map+0x2b1
  page_walk_handler+0x40
```
Priya: also seeing frequent "page table migration in progress" messages right before the faults. possible race between eviction and mapping update.
Jordan: any recent infra changes? kernel updates, nvidia-driver push, taint changes?
Alex: we applied kernel 6.4.12 -> 6.4.13 last night to gpu-node image; nvidia driver kept at 540. if this is a kernel-driver ABI problem, rollback kernel on a canary node might confirm.
Priya: agreed. I'll reproduce on a single node in lab by running heavy prefix-cache workloads and toggling page migration. if we can trigger locally we can capture full repro trace.
Maya: immediate mitigation: (1) cordon+drain impacted nodes (Alex), (2) shift traffic to fallback pool (Jordan), (3) increase node eviction thresholds to avoid cascade (infra-bot can apply), (4) get kernel-team looped (KernelTeam).
Alex: starting drain: `kubectl drain gpu-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — will failover pods to other pools.
infra-bot: applying temporary node eviction override on cluster: `kubectl patch cm cluster-config --patch '{"data":{"evictionThreshold":"45%"}}'` -> applied.
Jordan: routing policy updated: model-serving-route -> fallthrough to cpu-fallback and dedicated-reserve for critical tenants. traffic shift ~70% away from GPU pool.
Priya: repro attempt underway on lab-gpu-1. instrumenting with kgdb and enabling verbose GPU driver tracing. asking kernel team for specific tracepoints for page-walk handlers.
KernelTeam: joining thread — we saw similar European kernel trees showing page-walk interactions with large page tables and KSM. please capture mm_struct/migration timestamps.
Sam: notifying top impacted tenants with interim mitigation note: advising to expect occasional 502s while we mitigate. CS escalation to enterprise contacts done.
Maya: timeline and ownership: Priya (runtime lead) — root cause & repro, Alex (infra) — node drains/rollback, Jordan (oncall SRE) — traffic routing + interim SLOs, Sam (CS) — customer comms, KernelTeam — kernel trace.
Priya: initial hypothesis: kernel page table walker racing with driver eviction path causing stale PFN reads -> GPU page fault -> container oops. if confirmed we'll either roll kernel back or pin to older node image and plan a driver/kernel compatibility patch.
Jordan: mitigation checklist completed? need confirmation before we close P1.
Alex: drains done for gpu-03/04/05; nodes marked unschedulable and pods moved. one node (gpu-04) required a kubelet restart after driver recovered.
Priya: repro succeeded in lab: toggling migration while heavy KV cache workload triggers same PFN corruption. attaching snippet of reproduction steps in case we need to automate for other kernels.
```
# repro steps (lab):
1. start prefix-cache stress on lab-gpu-1
2. start concurrent OOM-triggering eviction routine (simulate host memory pressure)
3. toggle ksm and memory compaction: echo 1 > /sys/kernel/mm/ksm/run
4. observe page_walk PFN corruption in dmesg
```
Captured trace:
page_walk_handler+0x40
vm_migration_start+0x22
gpu_vm_unmap+0x1a
Priya: root cause ticket created in internal tracker: RT-8792 (kernel-driver page-walk race). adding tentative fix: driver-side lock around vm migration + coordination with kernel mm.
KernelTeam: we'll prioritize a kernel instrumentation patch to validate ordering, and coordinate with driver team for a short-term lock.
Sam: updated customer message: "We've detected a GPU node-level fault affecting a subset of on-demand model requests. We're actively mitigating by shifting traffic and restarting impacted nodes. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."
Maya: running post-mitigation checks now; error rate dropped to baseline for most tenants, 2 tenants still showing transient failures.
Jordan: closing actions: (A) patch infra to pin cluster image to kernel 6.4.12 for GPU pools, (B) KernelTeam + runtime to prepare driver lock patch, (C) create postmortem doc and include regression tests for migration+eviction, (D) schedule follow-up with product for SLA credits if needed.
Maya: thanks all — keep thread updated with repro PRs and timeline. switching to follow-up mode, leaving Priya as incident owner.
Priya: will post PRs and full logs here when ready.
infra-bot: incident INC-2134 status -> mitigated, monitoring.
Jordan: moving incident to postmortem queue.
Sam: final note: customers notified and CS will follow up individually for the two tenants with residual errors.
Maya: end-of-thread — great response.
